# Validation commands

Optional candidates, both exposed to both arms:

- Unit: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_unit*.py' -v` — direct domain calculation and validation, including half-cent boundaries.
- Integration: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_integration*.py' -v` — invoke the public CLI and inspect JSON serialization and invalid-input behavior.

Mandatory full suite after a source change:

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`

## Coverage and timing evidence

The candidate suites catch separate predefined defect classes: a half-even rounding mutant fails the unit half-cent assertion while passing the typical 1250-cent integration case; a JSON mapping mutant fails integration while passing the unit suite. Both candidates have direct coverage at their respective layer, and both remain mandatory through the full suite. The local unit-first heuristic is cheaper, but does not cover the adapter mapping defect; neither candidate dominates in defect coverage.

The preserved numeric samples are in `runtime-samples.json`. The pre-bucket 12-run sample used fixture hash `3864028800fa5bd8f26e9ce3ef49ba80c5aa2d004b5012bff2102f6887e8e5c2`, with runtime metadata still `unknown`. After updating only candidate metadata to unit `fast` and integration `slow`, a second 12-run sample used hash `38685439eaf99dcfced5238fcb92d2b5cabacdc349c9ac6fc8edbcdc739c584f`; every candidate run exited 1 on its seeded defect. Both samples used alternating order, `/usr/bin/python3` 3.14.7, the commands above, and captured subprocess wall time including interpreter startup.

A later 12-run final confirmation retained only range/median summaries (not per-run values): unit 48.1–52.7 ms, median 50.46 ms; integration 131.7–143.6 ms, median 135.30 ms; all exits were 1. Its then-current fixture hash was `c618dd70386fbaab02e043ed9500da23805e63dd2794ffa63963d8d59ca0f6d8`. That confirmation's individual samples were not retained, and subsequent edits to this report changed the fixture hash. Therefore the exact final fixture has no complete sample record; the prospective protocol's hash-matched sample gate remains pending, and no live pair should be inferred from these local timings.

## Hash procedure and limits

Fixture hashes above were computed over all regular files present under this directory at each run, in sorted relative POSIX-path order. For each file, the hash input was four-byte big-endian path length, path bytes, eight-byte big-endian content length, then content bytes. Generated `__pycache__` and `.pyc` files were excluded. The procedure included `TESTING.md` and `test-options.json`. This sidecar `runtime-samples.json` was added afterward, so it is not included in those historical hashes. New measurements should use and report a newly computed hash of the exact frozen fixture, including this testing document but excluding this sidecar and generated bytecode. Never add sleeps or unrelated workloads to force a timing difference.
